newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: One out of five Swiss women battered at home - study.
newsitem.headline: One out of five Swiss women battered at home - study.

text.p: One of every five women in Switzerland faces domestic violence from husbands or boyfriends, research published in a Swiss newspaper said on Wednesday.

The study in the French-language daily Tribune de Geneve said one out of eight women had suffered at least once from physical violence at home including beating, biting, kicking and punching and threats with a kitchen knife or even a weapon.
One in nine faced sexual abuse at home and two out of five suffered from psychological violence such as insults and threats, according to the Swiss National Scientific Research Fund study.
Swiss husbands or partners had "locked up" two out of five women at home at least once, the study said.
It gave no comparisons for previous years.
But it said domestic violence affected women from all walks of life in Switzerland, one of the world's richest countries, and that the subject remained a taboo in the male-dominated Swiss society.
Swiss women obtained the right to vote for the first time only in 1971.
Women's groups have since been fighting for civic rights and equality although their movement is mostly non-militant and rather tepid.

Tribune de Geneve said the results of the research would be a basis for a national equality campaign being launched by the government in the media and on television, accompanied by a telephone hotline for battered women.
It added that the German-speaking canton of Zurich had introduced a new method to deter domestic violence -- barring violent husbands and partners from their family circles.
